text:
For two periods and then some in Columbus, nobody scored. Cam Talbot and Casey DeSmith, two goalies who never heard their names called at a draft, kept turning chances away until the game finally needed a shootout to decide it.

DeSmith was the busier of the two in the most dangerous moments. His best stop came on a 45% chance for Mathieu Olivier in the third period, and he finished 29 of 30, saving 2.0 goals more than his shots deserved. Talbot stopped 27 of 28 and was 1.6 goals better than expected. The shot attempts were dead even, 62 apiece, and the expected goals (the quality of the chances) barely separated the teams, 2.96 for Columbus and 2.64 for Dallas.

Mikko Rantanen broke the deadlock at 6:27 of the third, from Wyatt Johnston, and Dallas went from a 48% win chance to 77%. The Stars held it deep into the period. Then, at 16:46, Zach Werenski scored on a backhand that our numbers gave a 5% chance, from Kent Johnson and Matthew Knies, and the Blue Jackets jumped from 10% to 52%. Werenski played 29 minutes and 24 seconds, put five shots on goal, and added 0.42 wins with that one shot, the most of anyone in the game.

Overtime solved nothing. In the shootout, Talbot stopped Jason Robertson and Tyler Seguin, DeSmith stopped Charlie Coyle, and Valeri Nichushkin and Johnson both beat DeSmith to win it. The Blue Jackets trailed in the third period and still won, and they deserved a slight edge over the full game, 56% of replays.

Dallas will feel this one. The Stars won 36 of 54 faceoffs, had the lead late, and got outstanding goaltending, yet left with one point after beating Columbus 3-1 on Oct. 31. If there is a concern for Dallas, it's 26 giveaways, a lot of free possessions to hand a team. For Columbus, it was a win built on patience and its goalie, and on Werenski finding a seam late.
headline: Talbot and DeSmith trade saves, and a shootout settles it
